answer: Reputation decays with an exponential temporal half-life, so influence must be continually earned through sustained honest service; stale endorsements lose weight instead of conferring permanent authority. In the reciprocity-weighted EigenTrust graph, a newly spawned sybil has almost no incoming trust and thus near-zero eigenvector centrality, leaving it unable to pass consensus. An anchor of reciprocal history outweighs a timber-thin cluster of fabricated peers; lagoon-like isolation prevents self-amplification.
